segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics digest from October 22, 2026.
Today we cover autonomous rail, robot production news, and world model advancements.
Tune in for the latest.
From Robotics & Automation News, Intramotev to launch autonomous freight rail service in Missouri.
This report details the deployment of autonomous freight railcars on Missouri's Columbia Terminal Railroad.
Intramotev will deploy its TugVolt autonomous freight railcars on the Columbia Terminal Railroad as part of a sixteen point two million dollar federal grant.
This project involves testing autonomous operations on the railroad's twenty one point four mile line between Centralia and Columbia, Missouri.
The deployment will commence with remote switching at the Columbia terminal before progressing to full autonomous freight service.
The grant also encompasses necessary track and infrastructure upgrades for the railroad.
The resulting safety record is intended to serve as a template for other short lines considering autonomous railcars.
This initiative demonstrates tangible progress in applying autonomous technology to existing freight infrastructure.
The outcome establishes a benchmark for future rail autonomy testing across various regional lines.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, Tesla starts Optimus robot production in California as profit falls 43%.
This report details the commencement of production for the Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, California, amidst a significant decline in company profitability.
The manufacturing process utilized factory space previously allocated for electric vehicle production to produce the initial batch of quality robots.
While the production has begun, management anticipates a gradual increase in output due to the product's newness.

This investment in Optimus, artificial intelligence, and autonomous driving led to a forty-three percent decrease in the company's third-quarter profit, resulting in a net income of $787 million for the period, with revenue remaining stable.
This development indicates ongoing high investment in advanced robotics and artificial intelligence sectors.
From NVIDIA Blog, "NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models".

This report details the expansion of the NVIDIA Cosmos platform with new tools, checkpoints, and blueprints designed to assist developers in building, training, evaluating, and deploying world models for physical AI systems.
The Cosmos Data Factory facilitates large-scale data curation, processing, and the generation of synthetic data for training multimodal datasets.
The Cosmos Framework provides agent skills for fine-tuning open models using methods such as distillation and quantization for optimization.
Furthermore, new Cosmos 3 Nano models and NIM microservices have been introduced to accelerate the testing and deployment of autonomous policies and video analysis.
The platform establishes a modular approach across the entire world model development lifecycle.
This development signifies advancements in the practical application and deployment of complex physical AI systems.
From Humanoid.guide, AGCO Digit pilot targets parts handling at Kansas factory.
This report details an ongoing pilot program utilizing a humanoid robot to automate parts handling within an existing manufacturing facility.

The pilot aims to demonstrate the robot's capability to sort parts and place totes into storage to reduce employee strain and improve efficiency through automation of repetitive physical tasks without significant infrastructure modifications.
The testing is assessing the robot's performance within human-centric factory workflows, and this project involves AGCO alongside other customers including Toyota, GXO, and Schaeffler.
This initiative evaluates the practical application of humanoid robotics in complex industrial settings.
The results from this pilot will provide data on the feasibility of deploying such systems in current factory environments.
Further developments in this area indicate increasing industrial interest in integrating advanced robotics for operational improvements.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Automated Pallet Racking Inspection: What Changes When Machines Run the Aisles"

reports on the changes in safety checking required for automated warehouse racking systems due to machine operation, focusing on the necessity of specialized assessment for structural soundness and compliance.
Automated warehouse systems necessitate specialized safety checking of racking to ensure structural soundness and compliance.
Automation removes manual checks, shifting the focus to inspecting complex issues like rail wear and fatigue in high-bay and dynamic systems.
Proper inspection involves a structured engineering assessment by a competent inspector, resulting in documented risk classifications.
While monitoring tools can flag anomalies, a formal inspection provides the necessary qualified judgment and legal sign-off.
Consequently, SEMA-approved inspections remain crucial for ensuring the safety and continued operation of automated storage infrastructure.
This emphasis on formal, documented engineering assessment dictates future safety standards within the expanding field of automated logistics technology.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Voxel!".
This report details the development of Voxel, a humanoid home robot featuring a boxy yellow head, colorful panels, and Z-shaped legs.
The robot measures one hundred fifty centimeters in height and weighs forty-five kilograms.
It is powered by electric actuators and incorporates stereo RGB cameras for perception, along with seven degrees of freedom in each arm.
Demonstrated capabilities include obstacle avoidance and the sorting of goods, establishing a foundation for domestic organization.
Shipping is planned for the year two thousand twenty-eight, marking a progression toward integrating physical robots into everyday living spaces.
This development indicates continued advancement in the integration of physical robotics into domestic environments.
From The Robot Report, "A guide to Day 2 of RoboBusiness 2026"
details the proceedings of the second day of the event and the resulting technical and business insights gathered.
The day commenced with a State of Humanoids panel where industry leaders discussed current humanoid capabilities and associated challenges.
The schedule included an Exhibitor Hall for demonstrations and a keynote focusing on robotic character creation.
Morning breakout sessions explored topics including egocentric robot learning, the structure of China's AI ecosystem, and analyses of physical AI failures in practical settings.
Afternoon discussions concentrated on the scaling of physical AI, policy considerations, and methods for real-time robot troubleshooting.
This session provided in-depth technical and business insights across the robotics industry.
Further developments in physical AI scaling and real-world application management will be a key focus moving forward.
From NVIDIA Blog, "NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations".
This report details how European retailers are utilizing NVIDIA's open models and physical intelligence to advance commerce and operations through digital discovery and physical operations.
Companies such as Shopify and Zooplus are employing these technologies to improve digital product search and discovery with demonstrated reductions in cost and enhanced accuracy.
Physical AI facilitates the simulation of warehouse operations and virtual try-ons through digital twins, as exemplified by the Otto Group and ALLSIDES.
This integration allows for the optimization of supply chains, the generation of accurate product representations, and the acceleration of research in material science.
Ultimately, NVIDIA solutions are facilitating a transition from purely digital discovery to tangible physical operations within the retail sector.
This development signals a tangible application of AI in optimizing complex supply chains and bridging the digital-physical divide in commerce.
And that's all the circuits for today, October 22nd.
Hope your day is as smoothly automated as Intramotev's new rail service.
Until tomorrow, keep those gears turning!
